editorial:
Imagine meeting a guy like Karthik, a fun youngster who is totally obsessed with astrology. He spends his days looking at stars and charts, trying to figure out the future. At first, you might think you are in for a quirky story about fate and predictions. When he and his buddy run into a shady drug dealer, the vibe shifts quickly. You expect a fast-paced crime thriller to kick in, but instead, you get a movie that feels like it forgot where it was going. The energy starts high but drops off fast, leaving you wondering why you are even watching.

Unfortunately, the acting is just okay and the plot goes nowhere. You will find yourself bored by the weak jokes and songs that do not fit the story. The production looks cheap, and the twists do not land with any punch. If you really want to give it a shot, you could try streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video or renting it on Apple TV to see if the visuals help. However, it is not a film you need to add to your 4K Blu-ray collection. Unless you are a huge fan of astrology, you can probably pass on this one.
endingExplained: The story ends on a very confusing note because the plot never really connects the astrology parts with the crime parts. After the trouble with the drug dealer, the movie tries to wrap things up with a few twists that do not make much sense. You see the characters resolve their conflict, but it feels rushed and empty. There is no big payoff, and the astrology theme is just dropped, leaving the ending feeling unfinished.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves experimental indie dramas with very slow pacing.
